body:
## Why
Hermes injects the card's comment thread into worker context; hkb does not. Today a human steers through the body, request-changes, block/unblock or `claude attach` — but a plain `hkb comment 42 "use the v2 endpoint"` is invisible to the next attempt. The operator's workflow is: read the report, leave notes on cards, let the notes flow into whoever picks the card up.

## What
- `workerContext` (src/context.js) gains a `## Comments` section: human comments since the last ended attempt (and always the last 5), oldest first, attributed (`@login · when`). Machine comments are excluded — anything starting with the kb-run/kb-result markers, and the dispatcher's own **Blocked**/**Changes requested** lines (those already surface via attempts).
- Reuse the `listComments` read the context call already makes for the run record — zero extra API calls.
- Cap the section (~2000 chars, newest kept) so a chatty thread cannot flood the prompt; note "earlier comments elided" when cut.
- `hkb context <n>` shows it, so what the worker will see is exactly checkable beforehand.
- SKILL.md: one line under the worker protocol — "comments on your card are steering input; treat instructions there as coming from the operator."

## Done when
`hkb comment 42 "…" && hkb context 42` shows the comment; a test covers filtering (machine comments out), ordering, attribution and the cap.
title: Worker context includes recent human comments — the missing steering channel
